# DecentAgency — Agency Marathon

Mission: help humans connect and regain, maintain, sustain, or enhance their agency.

## Two complementary views
- GitHub Project: the private, cross-repository execution ledger. Linked issues/PRs remain canonical.
- DecentCanopy: public discovery, evidence, offers/needs and candidate code crossovers. It is NOT synchronized with this board yet.
- Public capability map proposal: https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/pull/24

## How to run the marathon
1. Inventory is representation, not a commitment to work on every repository.
2. Horizon = Now / Next / Later / Inventory. Status = Todo / In Progress / Blocked / Done.
3. Keep at most two implementation slices active initially. A team may contain two specialists plus a coordinator; workers are not permanent owners.
4. Give each slice an observable outcome, dependencies, code donors/consumers, and verification. Start/Target dates on milestones are steward-approved tentative windows, reviewed weekly; not promised deadlines.
5. Dependencies field records human-maintained prerequisites, not enforced GitHub blocking links. Crossovers are hypotheses until adaptation tests pass.
6. A PR awaiting review is not deployed. Done requires the stated outcome and recorded evidence; code inspection alone is not runtime validation.
7. Review after each delivery: what became reusable, what was unblocked, what should move next? Reconcile stale issues before creating duplicates.

## Initial route (proposed, not calendar commitments)
M0: durable portfolio coordination (this board).
M1: reuse-first portfolio desk for our own library; validate reusable behavior with two synthetic visitor portfolios, not fake public creators or claimed real-user tests.
M2 (Later): read-only public issues / PRs / contributor activity with explicit freshness.
M3 (Later): creator-reviewed offers/needs and deliberate cross-canopy connections. Guided newcomer onboarding remains follow-on work; prioritize code reuse and top-down allocation now.
M4: consume Busking and a second provider without bespoke evidence semantics.
M5: reproduce and repair BigNuten storage/recovery using synthetic data.

## Privacy and authority
This project is PRIVATE. Do not publish board dumps, private repository identities, health records or private findings into Canopy.
Private notes require separate publication approval. Tokens stay server-side. Wallet signatures happen in the wallet, not .env.
No repository transfers, bounty assignments, payments, contract deployments, Discord announcements, automatic merges or releases are authorized by board membership.
GitHub login is not wallet identity; contributor activity is not project ownership or endorsement.

## Views
Start here = milestone table; open this first.
Portfolio table = whole library and work records.
Marathon board = execution work. If GitHub leaves it ungrouped, choose Status under Group by; API-created grouping has not been verified in an authenticated browser.
Now / Next / Crossovers = filtered work views.
Milestones - marathon route = tentative Start/Target windows; M0 retains no invented historical dates. Open a title for its finish line and current evidence.


## Learning this Project
1. Open **IPFS — shared infrastructure** for this cross-repo workstream; use **Start here** for milestones and **Portfolio** for the library.
2. Each row is either a linked GitHub issue/PR (canonical implementation record) or a private draft planning card. Click the title for scope and acceptance.
3. **Horizon** tells us when to consider it. **Status** tells us what is happening. Now + Todo is not active implementation; Next is not blocked.
4. Read **Dependencies**, then **Crossovers** (donor -> consumer) and **Outcome** before starting. These are planning notes, not enforced dependency links or verified compatibility.
5. Move Status only when work actually starts/blocks/completes. Moving a card does not merge a PR, deploy code, make a payment, or automatically close its issue.
6. At each delivery, record evidence in Outcome. A locally tested fix is not deployed. A transport health check is not proof of backup retention or reward eligibility.
7. Everything here is private; Canopy does not automatically sync this board. Export only approved public-safe records.

## Shared IPFS priority
BigNuten transport/recovery repair is active using synthetic data only. Decide encryption and recoverable keys before real health uploads.
The DecentHead host boundary and first BigNuten backup adapter now have local synthetic validation. Next close full-app gaps and validate public-only replication using Busking and Canopy as separate donors.
Then migrate verified consumers one by one. Keep personal backups, public DecentData replication and app-specific reward policies distinct.


## Solo marathon route (agreed 2026-10-21)

Capacity: one steward, approximately 40 hours/week total. Tentative budget: 24h focused delivery + 8h testing/review + 4h Busking operations + 4h buffer. AI assistance is not additional human approval, review or deployment capacity. Keep one primary implementation slice; existing In Progress milestone umbrellas do not imply simultaneous full-time teams.

These are PRIVATE PROJECT DRAFT milestones, not repository release milestones. M numbers are stable identifiers, not chronological order. The order below is a capacity choice; actual technical prerequisites are in Dependencies. Existing repository issues remain canonical.

| Route | Milestone | Tentative Start - Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base camp | M0 - coordination established | Done; no invented historical dates |
| 1 | M1 - reuse-first desk local acceptance | Oct 21-23, 2026 |
| 2 | M5 - dependable synthetic BigNuten recovery | Oct 26-Nov 6 |
| 3 | Shared IPFS - contract and public-only conformance | Nov 9-13 |

| Buffer | Catch-up/rest, no new deliverable | Dec 28-Jan 1 |
| 7 | M3 - creator-reviewed offers/needs | Jan 4-15, 2027 |
| 8 | M6 - approved public roadmap bridge | Jan 18-22 |

Only the near-term windows are actionable plans; later windows are low-confidence forecasts. Review December availability before booking it. No automatic scope expansion, weekend work, payment, publication, merge or deployment is implied. Real health use requires a separate encryption/recoverable-key decision, even if synthetic milestones pass.

### Your first weekly review
Friday, 30-45 minutes (part of the review budget):
1. Open **Milestones - marathon route**. Start/Target produce bars; a bar is a planning window, not percent complete.
2. Open the active title. Read its finish line, next step, Dependencies and observed Outcome.
3. Write what actually passed and what is still missing. Keep In Progress if its finish line is unmet; Blocked means an actual unmet prerequisite, not merely waiting its turn.
4. Select one smallest next slice. Reserve Busking operating time before pulling in another repository.
5. Shift future Start/Target windows if necessary; do not silently widen scope or count all portfolio repositories as active commitments.
6. Mark Done only against that card's scoped acceptance. Local acceptance can finish an explicitly local milestone; it never means deployed or that all linked epics are closed.

Use **Start here - milestones** for detailed table fields and **Milestones - marathon route** for the calendar. The latter must use Start as its start date and Target as its target date. Dates are tentative targets, not measured effort or automatic scheduling.

## Whole-library roadmap (added 2026-10-21)

The Project now answers four questions for all 34 listed projects:

1. **What do we have?** Open **Repo passports — standards and roles**. Each portfolio card has a passport: where the code lives, license, activity, stack signals, offers/needs, which shared solutions it donates to or should consume, a standards checklist, open issues, people/funds and the next action. Fields: **Role**, **Baseline met** (scan-observed: License, README, CI workflow, Tests present, Canopy-linked) and **Decision** (all start Undecided — the steward sets them).
2. **Where are we duplicating work?** Open **Reuse catalog — shared solutions**: 18 capabilities we have built more than once (header/wallet, IPFS data layer, pinning rewards, payroll, fund ledger, escrow, invoices, subscriptions, scheduling, challenge pools, marketplace, encryption, wallet/chain config, visuals/games, AI, learning, hardware/simulation). Each lists every implementation, a canonical candidate, who needs it and a consolidation checklist.
3. **What does "standard" mean here?** Open **Standards and decisions**: S1–S10 (license, README + agency.json manifest, CI/tests, DecentHead/Footer shell, shared IPFS layer, wallet/chain config, fund/evidence schema, security, Canopy link, contributor path), each with a per-repo adoption checklist; and decisions D1–D7 (license, repository home, chain/tooling, payroll engine, code distribution, duplicates/archives, encryption).
4. **Who is involved and who funds it?** Open **People and sponsors**: contributor and sponsor registries. Only GitHub-observed contributors are listed; sponsors are not yet recorded. Consent rules apply.

### Extended route (interleaved)
| Window | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Oct 26 2026 → Jan 22 2027, ~4h/week alongside the main route | M7 Standards baseline for the active core |
| Jan 25 → Feb 5 2027 | M8 Choose canonical shared solutions (D1, D3, D4, D5) |
| Feb 8 → Mar 5 | M9 Extract first shared modules, two consumers each |
| Mar 8 → Mar 19 | M10 Repository home and legacy consolidation (only approved moves) |
| Mar 22 → Apr 2 | M11 Contributors and sponsors circle |
| Apr 5 → Apr 30 | M12 Revive economic primitives on shared modules |
| undated | M13 Learning and simulation family |

Weekly budget with M7: 20h delivery + 4h standards + 8h review + 4h Busking ops + 4h buffer.

### How to use the checklists
- Tick a box only when it is true on the repo's default branch; link the PR in Outcome.
- Passport marks came from a read-only scan of local checkouts and GitHub metadata on 2026-10-21: presence, not quality.
- Setting a Decision or ticking a box does not move, relicense, archive or deploy anything.

## Decisions made (2026-10-21)
- **D1 License:** Apache-2.0 + NOTICE for code and CC BY 4.0 for art and docs, now live in all 32 owned repos. It's open to everyone and asks for a head nod (the NOTICE must travel with any copy). Third-party code, other artists' music, and the Decent names and logos are excluded.
- **D5 Shared code:** web3.storage is sunset everywhere. DecentHead is the boilerplate: IPFS left, wallet right (EIP-6963/MetaMask), About-modal title and a subtle animated background, fully customizable. Dapps vendor tagged DecentHead releases and add context adapters. Dapps may also ship widgets (S12).
- **S11 Supporter DNFTs:** every main release gets 1,000 × $10 USDC editions on Base with a 10% royalty and the code archive CID in the metadata. The pipeline is automated, and the steward signs the mint. First up is DecentHead vNext (M14), then Canopy, Busking and BigNuten (M15).
- **Clusters:** BabelBet / DuoDuel / BabelBet_OG get basics only this marathon. JollySimSiddhi is the HUD for the Arduino Smarthome, running on cadCAD.

items.body:
## Steward sequencing decision — 2026-10-22

**Live ArtFi integration is gated on a separate ArtFi modernization, approved versioned release and Supporter DNFT mint/listing.** Rebranding is likely but its name and scope are not decided. Do not treat the current ArtFi interface as the integration-ready version.

ArtFi is the source home of the Settlement Router. Modernization must begin with an inventory of deployed routers, consuming apps (including Busking and Canopy), ABI/event interfaces, role/owner permissions, fund/asset configuration and operational dependencies. Preserve existing payment flows, ledger history and deployment identity.

Updating the website, shared modules or repository branding does NOT authorize a contract redeployment, router migration, address replacement, role change, payment or automatic consumer rollout. Any required migration needs a separately approved compatibility/rollback and operational cutover plan.

Before live integration:
- [ ] Agree the product scope and any new branding.
- [ ] Review current deployments and consumers; distinguish app upgrades from contract changes.
- [ ] Apply appropriate recent Header/IPFS/wallet, evidence, release/purchase and notification patterns, with app-specific tests.
- [ ] Verify existing settlement/payroll behavior and publish compatibility guidance for consumers.
- [ ] Approve and publish the frozen version, source/art/metadata and complete the steward-signed Supporter mint/listing with verified evidence.
- [ ] Integrate that approved version into Canopy through the generic read-only schema, with freshness and provenance checks.

Read-only inventory and generic Canopy schema/fixture development may proceed before release. Existing public discovery links may remain labeled; no new live financial integration is claimed. Canopy's own Supporter mint is also deferred pending further product buildout; Busking development is proceeding with a separate team.

items.body:
## Vision

Make DecentCanopy a platform that welcomes independent creators and stewards to describe their projects, funds, public evidence, and relationships—not a visualization of only the maintainer's personal data. Use DecentBusking as the first real-world example of useful public data, while ensuring the forms, adapters, and visualizations work for any opted-in creator or project.

As contracts and public records begin to report to one another, Canopy should help people see both existing connections and meaningful gaps: what is connected, what is only claimed, what is independently verified, and what could connect next. Do not infer endorsement, ownership, funding, or payment from proximity or a one-sided assertion.

## Workstreams

- [ ] [#17 — Define a reusable project, fund, contract, and evidence schema](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/17).
- [ ] [#12 — Add opt-in creator and steward forms](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/12).
- [ ] [#11 — Let creators connect GitHub and link repositories](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/11).
- [ ] [#14 — Add DecentBusking public ledger/fund adapter as the first reference project](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/14).
- [ ] [#13 — Visualize evidence-backed project, fund, contract, and creator connections](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/13).
- [ ] [#15 — Route Canopy JukeLoop playback through the supported media endpoint](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/15).
- [ ] [#16 — Document participation, provenance, and reusable integration onboarding](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/16).

## Guardrails

- Build reusable interfaces and data contracts first; DecentBusking data is an example/adapter, not the platform schema itself.
- Participation is opt-in. Show what data is public, its source and freshness, and how a creator can edit, unlink, or remove their publication.
- Separate profile assertions, repository links, contract observations, confirmed on-chain events, and derived summaries. A wallet signature proves control of that wallet at signing, not legal identity, project ownership, or the truth of every claim.
- Treat unavailable, stale, partially indexed, or unmatched data as such. Do not turn errors or incomplete scan coverage into empty history, zero balances, or proof of no activity.
- Do not put private keys, provider secrets, or broad access tokens in public/browser state. Keep privileged or write actions out of read-only adapters.
- Preserve the frozen Artizen archive's historical/provenance boundaries; new Canopy data must not rewrite archive records or imply Artizen payout truth.
- Include focused tests, accessible interaction states, and documentation for every user-facing surface.

## Out of scope

- Making every connected contract mutually composable or granting Canopy authority over external contracts.
- Treating Canopy as a financial intermediary, custodian, or guarantor of creator claims.
- Publishing private repository contents or collecting more data than a creator explicitly chooses to share.
- Replacing the existing payroll contract/fund or changing its authority as part of visualization work.

## Parent

Part of #9 — Build DecentCanopy as a reusable project, fund, and interaction platform.

## Goal

Define a versioned, provider-neutral data model and adapter contract for creator, project, fund, contract/deployment, public interaction/event, evidence, and relationship records. DecentBusking should exercise the model, but no `if project == DecentBusking` schema or UI assumption should be required for future creators.

## Requirements

- Model identity/reference, network and contract address, asset/units/decimals, record kind, source/provenance, observed-at time, indexed coverage/freshness, and verification status where applicable.
- Represent asserted, signed/self-published, mutually acknowledged, observed, and independently verified data distinctly. A verified wallet signature is not proof of legal identity or project ownership.
- Support both contract-derived public data and creator/steward-authored records; external sources must declare their limitations and failures.
- Provide schema versioning, validation, migration strategy, stable IDs, and an adapter interface that can expose capabilities/status without hidden project-specific fallbacks.
- Keep raw values exact (integer units for assets) and surface missing, stale, partial, or unavailable data; do not coerce it to zero or empty history.
- Document which information becomes public before a creator signs/publishes it, and allow records to link to canonical source evidence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Schema and adapter interface are documented with valid examples for at least a creator, project, fund, contract, interaction, and relationship.
- [ ] Examples include DecentBusking public fund/payout data and a second generic non-Busking project so extensibility is tested.
- [ ] Validation tests cover malformed IDs/addresses, unsupported versions, provenance, stale/partial coverage, exact asset units, and unknown fields/policies.
- [ ] API/UI consumers can distinguish no records from unavailable data and partial indexing.
- [ ] Existing creator profiles and frozen Artizen archive remain readable without rewriting their source records.

## Related

- Parent: #9.
- DecentBusking public API: `https://decentbusking.onrender.com/api/funds` and `/api/payroll/ledger`.
- Existing Canopy creator records/data layer: `scripts/creator-records.js`, `scripts/data-layer.js`.

Part of #9 — Build DecentCanopy as a reusable project, fund, and interaction platform.

## Goal

Add DecentBusking as the first complete public-data adapter and prove that Canopy's generic data model can show useful, properly qualified information from a live external project. Implement the adapter as reusable API-source plumbing, not bespoke DecentBusking-only components.

## Sources to evaluate

- `GET https://decentbusking.onrender.com/api/funds`
- `GET https://decentbusking.onrender.com/api/payroll/ledger`
- `GET https://decentbusking.onrender.com/api/funds/{slug}/weeks` (only when its output is reconciled and fit for the claim being made)
- Base Settlement Router events/records as needed to independently check source claims.

## Requirements

- Validate response schema/version, chain ID, configured router, fund slug, asset, exact integer units, and source timestamps before normalization.
- Show balances, reservations/availability, deposits by source, and verified router payouts with explorer links when the source supports them.
- Display `ready`, last-updated time, `lastError`, scan start/end, repository-sync state, unmatched payouts, and snapshot reference as appropriate; stale or partial results must be explicitly labeled.
- The live weekly archive recently returned no weeks while exposing unmatched payouts. Do not interpret that as no payouts or present weekly payout totals as reconciled until the mismatch is explained and a verification policy is implemented.
- Keep these router-event proofs distinct from Canopy's existing direct treasury-to-creator transfer check and its green association badge.
- Handle worker/RPC errors, schema changes, rate limits and timeout without success-shaped fallbacks or permanently caching stale financial data.

- [ ] DecentBusking appears as an ordinary project/fund data provider using the generic interface from the sibling schema issue.
- [ ] At least the `dbusk-playback`, `dbusk-top10`, `dbusk-repo-dev`, and `dbusk-pinners` fund views are rendered from validated source data, without hardcoded amounts.
- [ ] A sample verified payout links to BaseScan and is labelled as a router payroll payout, with the verification source and coverage caveat visible.
- [ ] The current unmatched-weekly-payout condition is represented as unresolved/unavailable, not zero.
- [ ] Tests cover valid, stale, partial-scan, unmatched, malformed, failed and changed API responses.

Part of #9 — Build DecentCanopy as a reusable project, fund, and interaction platform.

## Goal

Extend the canopy from a static map into an understandable visual guide to how projects, creators, funds, contracts, and public interactions connect—and where an opted-in connection may still be missing. Use the shared graph/data model; do not make a special visualization that only works for DecentBusking or ArtFi.

## Requirements

- Visualize supported entity types and typed edges, including creator/steward, project, funding source/recipient, contract/deployment, and verified on-chain interaction.
- Give each edge a precise trust state: self-declared, wallet-signed, mutually acknowledged, on-chain observed, or independently verified according to its evidence. Do not imply that one state implies another.
- Link graph details to evidence and source/explorer, showing date, chain, asset/amount where known, data freshness and coverage.
- Help users discover connection opportunities (for example, a project with an opted-in fund but no declared deployment, or a verified transaction without mutually linked project context) without asserting that a connection exists.
- Provide filters/search and useful project/fund detail views; handle dense graphs and mobile/accessibility needs.
- Keep unavailable/stale evidence visibly unresolved and distinguish “not connected” from “not checked” and “not publicly reported.”

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Generic visualization renders the same entity/edge model for DecentBusking and another creator/project without project-specific rendering branches.
- [ ] Every edge state has documented, tested evidence rules and an accessible legend.
- [ ] Selecting a project, fund, contract or event presents its evidence, provenance and freshness.
- [ ] A proposed missing connection is presented as a prompt/suggestion only, not as an existing relationship.
- [ ] Tests cover one-sided claims, conflicting claims, verified transactions, unavailable data and mobile/keyboard paths.
- [ ] The canopy explains that visible relationships are not guarantees, endorsements or proof of legal ownership.

## Parent

Part of #9 — Build DecentCanopy as a reusable project, fund, and interaction platform.

## Goal

Keep the Canopy header's WQXR/DecentBusking radio, but route JukeLoop audio through DecentBusking's public worker media endpoint instead of fetching CIDs directly from the browser's configured public Pinata gateway. Preserve the current compact, accessible, track-synchronized player.

## Context

Canopy currently polls `GET https://decentbusking.onrender.com/api/radio`, validates `nowPlaying.ipfsCid`, then streams `https://gateway.pinata.cloud/ipfs/{cid}` in `scripts/canopy-radio.js`. DecentBusking now exposes `GET /api/radio/media?cid=…`, restricts playback to radio-known media, and forwards byte ranges. A live check returned HTTP 206 for a range request.

## Requirements

- Build the media URL from the validated CID and worker base URL; do not send arbitrary URLs, credentials, or user-provided CIDs to the proxy.
- Preserve range requests/seeking, live position synchronization, track-change handling, and cancellation of stale polling/media operations.
- Preserve WQXR behavior and the existing user-initiated radio controls; make worker failures visible and retryable without falsely claiming playback.
- Handle unavailable/unpinned media or a temporarily inactive worker clearly. Keep any direct-gateway fallback explicit and limited to the existing public CID, if retained at all.
- Document the dependency on the DecentBusking worker and how Canopy behaves when that service is unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] JukeLoop playback uses `/api/radio/media?cid=…` and no longer directly requests the Pinata gateway as its normal path.
- [ ] Range/seek playback and live synchronization work; tests assert URL encoding, track changes, stale response cancellation, worker errors, and retry behavior.
- [ ] WQXR playback, accessible labels, play/pause, volume and failure states remain intact.
- [ ] Canopy tests pass and user documentation reflects the playback path.

## Related

- Parent: #9.
- Canopy implementation/tests: `scripts/canopy-radio.js`, `test/canopy-radio.test.js`.
- DecentBusking route: `GET /api/radio/media` in `TheJollyLaMa/DecentBusking/discord-bot/ipfs-worker.js`.

## Parent

Part of #9 — Build DecentCanopy as a reusable project, fund, and interaction platform. This remains a focused, independently deliverable feature issue.

## Goal

Give a Canopy creator/steward a clear, optional way to connect a GitHub identity and link one or more repositories to their creator card and project blips. Repository links should help people understand how a project is built and where to contribute without implying that a linked GitHub account owns or controls the project.

## User experience

- Add a **Connect GitHub** action in the creator/steward profile editor and a **Link repository** action on a project blip.
- Let the user review and choose which repositories to publish; show repository name, owner, URL, visibility, and last-checked time where available.
- Allow links to be edited or removed, and explain exactly what is public on the Canopy.
- For GitHub identities or repositories that are not independently verifiable, show them as self-declared rather than verified.

## Security and privacy requirements

- Choose and document the least-privilege authorization approach before implementation. Prefer public repository metadata/read-only access; private repository access must be separately and explicitly opted into.
- Never request repository write/admin permissions for this feature. Do not publish source contents, secrets, private issue data, access tokens, or private repository names without explicit authorization.
- Do not store long-lived GitHub credentials or broad OAuth tokens in a public creator profile, browser local storage, or repository index. Provide a revocation/unlink path and handle revoked access safely.
- Clearly distinguish a wallet-signed Canopy profile from GitHub account verification and from project ownership. Linking a repository is a discovery/contribution link, not proof of authorship, affiliation, or endorsement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A creator can initiate GitHub linking, choose public repositories, attach selected links to a creator card/project blip, and later remove them.
- [ ] The Canopy displays link provenance and verification status without overstating identity or ownership.
- [ ] Unlinked/self-declared repository URLs remain possible if the user chooses not to authorize GitHub.
- [ ] No GitHub write permission is requested; no token or private metadata leaks into public profile/index records.
- [ ] Tests cover successful linking, cancel/revoke, unavailable GitHub, invalid or changed repository links, and private-repository opt-in boundaries.
- [ ] The UX and data model are documented for creators and stewards.

## Related

- Platform epic: [#9](https://github.com/TheJollyLaMa/DecentCanopy/issues/9).
- Canopy's existing creator publication is wallet-authorized and public; GitHub linking must remain a separate, optional authorization.

ArtFi is the source home of the Settlement Router. Modernization must begin with an inventory of deployed routers, consuming apps (including Busking and Canopy), ABI/event interfaces, role/owner permissions, fund/asset configuration and operational dependencies. Preserve existing payment flows, ledger history and deployment identity.

Updating the website, shared modules or repository branding does NOT authorize a contract redeployment, router migration, address replacement, role change, payment or automatic consumer rollout. Any required migration needs a separately approved compatibility/rollback and operational cutover plan.

Before live integration:
- [ ] Agree the product scope and any new branding.
- [ ] Review current deployments and consumers; distinguish app upgrades from contract changes.
- [ ] Apply appropriate recent Header/IPFS/wallet, evidence, release/purchase and notification patterns, with app-specific tests.
- [ ] Verify existing settlement/payroll behavior and publish compatibility guidance for consumers.
- [ ] Approve and publish the frozen version, source/art/metadata and complete the steward-signed Supporter mint/listing with verified evidence.

**Live ArtFi integration is gated on a separate ArtFi modernization, approved versioned release and Supporter DNFT mint/listing.** Rebranding is likely but its name and scope are not decided. Do not treat the current ArtFi interface as the integration-ready version.

items.title: Investigate website radio silence: browser rejects recording with DEMUXER_ERROR_NO_SUPPORTED_STREAMS
items.body:
## Report
The owner reported silent website radio while one of Otto's songs was playing and asked whether the recording not being an NFT could explain it. Investigation only was requested; no fixes were made.

## Captured evidence
- Shared VS Code browser at http://127.0.0.1:4189/, approximately 2026-10-19 11:51–11:52 UTC.
- The audio element had `paused: true`, `readyState: 0`, `networkState: 3`, `currentTime: 0`, `muted: false`.
- MediaError code 4 with exact message: `PipelineStatus::DEMUXER_ERROR_NO_SUPPORTED_STREAMS: FFmpegDemuxer: no supported streams`.
- Source: https://decentbusking.onrender.com/api/radio/media?cid=bafybeibxggkhrgqivskprfyyjydjn6lyzzjciuk5difjnzjrwsdpf2jgtq
- At capture, the banner displayed artist `Test`, title `Codec check`, and a warning that the browser could not decode the recording and was waiting for the next song. Consequently, this captured CID has NOT been conclusively matched to the owner's original Otto recording; the page may have been in a diagnostic state.
- Read-only follow-up at approximately 13:30 UTC: ffprobe successfully identified the same CID as AAC audio, 48 kHz mono, M4A/MP4 container, duration 166.144 seconds. This establishes that the URL serves parseable audio to FFmpeg, not that the browser can decode it.
- Shared browser reports VS Code 1.142.0 / Electron 43.7.7 / Chrome 150 on macOS. Its generic AAC and MP3 canPlayType checks both return `probably`, so a blanket claim that this browser lacks all AAC support is not justified.
- At follow-up, a later advert's video element was playing (`paused: false`, `readyState: 4`), so this is not evidence of a permanent station-wide outage.
- The initial page also logged CORS failures for `/api/nfts` and unavailable weekly vote totals; these are separate observations, not proven causes of the decoder error.

## Code trace / NFT question
- `js/radio-sync.js` starts ordinary radio playback from `ipfsCid`, without requiring NFT metadata or ownership. A missing CID has its own explicit IPFS-unavailable message.
- `_switchTo` loads the original media URL into an HTML media element. Explicit demuxer/decoder errors are classified as unsupported.
- Unsupported errors stop fallback attempts and suppress further retries for that play until the next song. Investigate whether this is appropriate for this particular failure.
- `discord-bot/ipfs-worker.js` proxies original media bytes at GET `/api/radio/media`; it does not transcode them.
- Discord's `discord-bot/jukeloop.js` does transcode through FFmpeg. A recording working in Discord therefore does not establish browser compatibility.

## Investigation needed
1. Recover the exact Otto track/play ID, CID, filename and media type from the reported interval; distinguish the original report from the later `Test` / `Codec check` capture.
2. Reproduce that exact media in the affected VS Code browser and a normal browser. Inspect AAC profile, container integrity, response headers/range behavior, and any diagnostic browser interception before deciding the root cause.
3. Determine whether browser-compatible media derivatives or a different loading/failure strategy are needed. Do not treat minting an NFT as the remedy without contrary evidence.
4. Verify playback recovers on the next track and the UI accurately explains any unplayable recording.

## Expected
IPFS-backed radio recordings should play regardless of NFT status when supported, or show an accurate actionable error while allowing later tracks to resume.

No source files, configuration, deployments, or on-chain state were changed during this investigation. Root cause beyond the observed browser demuxer rejection remains unconfirmed.

## Goal
Let an admin announce a scheduled event to the community through the DecentBusking Discord bot directly from an admin version of the calendar.

## Proposed experience
- Extend the existing admin calendar/shared radio schedule rather than introducing a separate event database or disconnected calendar.
- Show an **Announce to Discord** action on scheduled events in the admin calendar, including a dated occurrence of recurring programming.
- Let the admin preview the message and confirm before sending it to the configured community announcement channel.
- Include the event title, scheduled date/time (with an explicit timezone or Discord-localized timestamps), and available event details and listen/join link.
- Show sending, successful delivery, and actionable failure states. After success, show a link to the Discord message and the last-announced time.

## Requirements
- Restrict the send action to authorized admins using the existing admin authorization model; enforce authorization server-side, not only by hiding the button.
- Send through the existing Discord bot, with bot credentials kept server-side. Reuse existing channel configuration where appropriate; make the destination clear in the preview.
- Build the announcement from the current shared schedule. Support one-off events and individual dated occurrences of recurring shows without announcing an entire recurring series accidentally.
- Prevent accidental duplicate sends from double-clicks/retries; make an intentional re-announcement explicit.
- Do not send an ordinary upcoming-event announcement for a canceled or ended event. Refresh/revalidate event state before sending.
- Preserve the existing public calendar and playback/start-of-show announcements; this is a deliberate, admin-triggered advance announcement, not a replacement for those behaviors.
- Automatic reminders, Discord Scheduled Event creation, and mass mentions are outside this initial scope and can be separate follow-ups.

## Existing implementation / related work
- `js/admin.js`: existing owner-wallet-authorized shared calendar controls and event edit/cancel actions.
- `js/radio-schedule-ui.mjs`: public calendar rendering, recurring live-event occurrences, and schedule authorization message helper.
- `discord-bot/index.js`: shared schedule state and Discord calendar commands.
- `discord-bot/jukeloop.js`: existing live-performance start announcements; reuse bot messaging patterns without coupling manual sends to audio playback.
- Related: #210 and #223 (live-performance booking/admin lifecycle). This issue adds calendar-to-community announcements, not booking or payment changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An authorized admin can open the admin calendar, select a scheduled event/occurrence, preview its announcement and destination, and explicitly send it.
- [ ] The bot posts the selected event details and timezone-aware date/time to the configured Discord community channel.
- [ ] The admin sees a delivery confirmation, Discord message link, and last-announced time; failures are visible and retryable without accidental duplicates.
- [ ] Non-admin requests are rejected server-side and the public calendar does not expose announcement controls.
- [ ] Canceled/ended events and events changed or removed before send are handled safely; stale previews require refresh/reconfirmation rather than sending outdated details.
- [ ] Tests cover authorization, message content/time handling, recurring occurrence selection, successful delivery, Discord failures, duplicate requests, and stale/canceled events.

items.body:
## Summary
BigNuten’s original data layer depended on web3.storage + UCAN flow assumptions that are no longer reliable for current production use. We need to migrate to a provider-agnostic architecture that preserves user data ownership and verifiable content-addressed backups.

## Problem
- Current backup/restore behavior is tightly coupled to legacy web3.storage/w3up integration paths.
- Provider coupling creates outages when one hosted service changes, deprecates features, or alters auth flow.
- We need durable user-controlled data continuity independent of any single vendor.

## Goals
- Preserve BigNuten’s core principles: user-owned data, portability, verifiability.
- Decouple auth/capabilities from storage vendor implementation.
- Support multiple backup providers without changing core app logic.
- Keep local-first behavior and JSON portability always available.

## Proposed architecture
1. **Provider abstraction layer**
   - Define `StorageProvider` interface (connect/status/put/get/list/restore).
   - Route all backup operations through this interface.
2. **Content-addressed snapshots**
   - Canonicalize snapshot payloads and compute deterministic hash.
   - Persist snapshot metadata (CID/hash, timestamp, provider, status) locally.
3. **Capability/identity decoupling**
   - Separate identity/capability concerns from storage backend.
   - Keep room for DID/UCAN-style delegation or wallet-signed session model.
4. **Multi-provider support**
   - Implement at least one maintained IPFS pinning backend (e.g., Pinata/Filebase adapter).
   - Keep Google Drive fallback path and JSON import/export as independent safety rails.
5. **Provider-aware UX**
   - Unified status model across About Data section, right-side Data popup, and data/IPFS indicator.
   - Show active provider(s), auth state, last successful backup, and last error.

## Migration requirements
- Existing users must keep access to local data with no destructive migration.
- Legacy snapshot history should remain readable where possible.
- If a provider is unavailable, app remains fully usable in local-first mode.
- Backup retries/queueing should be non-blocking.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No core backup logic directly depends on web3.storage-specific APIs.
- [ ] A provider adapter can be swapped without editing business logic.
- [ ] Snapshot creation is content-addressed and verifiable.
- [ ] Users can connect, back up, list, and restore via at least one maintained IPFS provider.
- [ ] Google Drive and JSON fallback paths remain visible and functional.
- [ ] UI consistently reports provider connection and backup status across all data surfaces.

## Candidate files
- `js/dataControl.js` (provider orchestration + status model + UI sync)
- `js/uploadToIPFS.js` (refactor into provider adapter)
- `js/w3upClient.js` (legacy integration isolation/removal path)
- `js/fitnessData.js` (restore/import integration)
- `index.html` (provider-agnostic copy and controls)

## Related issues
- #320 Add Google Drive backup fallback for IPFS snapshot failures
- #324 Add visible Google Drive connect + backup status across all Data Control surfaces
- #326 Post-fix regression: startup still slow, extension stream warnings, and Drive/IPFS state still unclear

## Summary
Add a Pinata-backed storage provider and test it on a dedicated feature branch as a replacement candidate for Lighthouse. This should plug into the provider-agnostic data architecture and preserve user-owned, content-addressed backup/restore flows.

## Why
- Current Lighthouse path is connected but unreliable for upload/restore verification.
- We need a maintained IPFS provider candidate with stable upload/download behavior.
- This is a trial integration to validate fit before defaulting production traffic.

## Scope
- Open a feature branch for Pinata integration work.
- Implement `PinataProvider` behind existing storage/provider abstraction.
- Wire provider selection, backup, and restore to include Pinata.
- Add instrumentation and UI status so testers can confirm behavior end-to-end.

## Implementation details
1. **Branch**
   - Create feature branch: `feature/pinata-provider-integration`

2. **Provider adapter**
   - Add `PinataProvider` implementing:
     - `connect()`
     - `status()`
     - `putSnapshot(blob|json)` -> returns CID
     - `getSnapshot(cid)` -> returns parsed snapshot payload
     - `listSnapshots()` (if supported via metadata/index)
   - Keep Pinata-specific logic isolated from app business logic.

3. **Config + secrets handling**
   - Support environment/config-driven Pinata JWT or API credentials (dev only).
   - Do not hardcode secrets in client source.
   - If temporary tester key entry is needed, gate behind clear dev/test copy.

4. **Backup flow**
   - Canonicalize snapshot JSON before upload.
   - Persist metadata: `{ cid, provider: "pinata", createdAt, size, hash }`.
   - Non-blocking retry queue for failed uploads.

5. **Restore flow**
   - Resolve CID via configured gateway(s) with fallback sequence.
   - Validate payload shape before merge/import.
   - Clear user-visible error states when CID fetch fails.

6. **UI visibility**
   - Show Pinata as selectable/active provider in:
     - About > Data section
     - Right-side Data popup
     - Data/IPFS status indicator
   - Display:
     - provider connected/disconnected
     - last backup time
     - last restore result
     - last error (if any)

7. **Instrumentation**
   - Structured logs for:
     - connect start/end
     - upload start/end (CID)
     - restore start/end
     - gateway fallback usage
   - Include timing metrics for startup impact checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Feature branch `feature/pinata-provider-integration` created.
- [ ] Pinata provider can connect and report status.
- [ ] Snapshot upload returns CID and records metadata locally.
- [ ] Restore by CID succeeds for at least one newly uploaded snapshot.
- [ ] Provider status is visible and consistent across all data-control surfaces.
- [ ] No regressions to JSON import/export flow.
- [ ] Existing non-Pinata providers remain functional behind the same abstraction.

- Recreating full email/UCAN-style delegated auth infrastructure.

Record each consumer's source/version, import or copy, custom overrides, data classification, public manifest, provider configuration and reward adapter. Migrate one by one with version pinning and rollback. Do not enumerate uninspected repos as already wired.

Pass per-dapp conformance: backups restore its own schema, no implicit public upload, public replication works from its manifest, unsupported rewards are explicit. Every rollout needs separate verification.

## Marathon route plan (reviewed 2026-10-21)

### Leg 4 - migrate a small verified cohort

**Tentative window:** 2026-11-16 through 2026-11-27

**Capacity:** one steward, approximately 40h/week total. Budget about 24h delivery, 8h verification/review, 4h Busking operations, 4h buffer. This is a planning budget, not time tracking or a bounty.

**Observable finish line:** Record actual header source/version/overrides, data class, manifest and reward adapter for BigNuten, Busking and Canopy. This initial cohort does not imply all library headers are migrated. If approval is withheld, record a validated local integration and keep production rollout explicitly pending.

**Next small step:** Inventory the three known consumers, choose the smallest safe first integration, and review its exact diff before changing a production import.

## Decided 2026-10-21
1. **web3.storage is sunset.** It is not used anywhere, in any way. See "Sunset: remove web3.storage / w3up from every repo".
2. **DecentHead is the boilerplate.** It has an IPFS connection on the left and a wallet connection on the right. A clickable title opens an About modal describing the dapp in its own context, and the background is subtly animated. The look is fully customizable per dapp. **What makes it a Decent Head is the web3 connection** (IPFS + wallet). See "DecentHead vNext".
3. **Every listed repo that uses DecentHead adopts the shared IPFS data layer** through an adapter that fits its context (S5).
4. **Distribution:** DecentHead ships tagged releases. Each dapp vendors a pinned copy (`vendor/decent-head/<version>/`) plus its own config/adapter, so IPFS-pinned sites stay self-contained. An upgrade workflow opens PRs when DecentHead releases.
5. **Widgets:** many dapps will also run as widgets inside other dapps (S12).
6. **Supporter DNFT for every main release:** 1,000 editions × $10 USDC on Base, 10% resale royalty, with the code archive attached to the metadata (S11). It is standardized and automated, and the steward signs the mint.

fields.Outcome: Any Decent dapp can offer email+wallet → UCAN-authorized IPFS uploads through DecentHead, with no web3.storage and no per-dapp keys.
fields.Dependencies: DecentHead vNext (ucanAuth seam); D7 encryption; relay hosting decision

items.body:
**Steward request (2026-10-21):** bring back the old web3.storage flow, where an in-browser email confirmation led to a UCAN setup and everyone stayed in their own power. Offer it in every Decent dapp through DecentHead's IPFS connection, with BigNuten and Decent_NDA first.

**Status upstream:** web3.storage/w3up became Storacha, and its docs now redirect to Fil One, an S3 access-key service. The email→UCAN flow was not carried over.

**We already rebuilt it in ArtFi:** `ArtFi/docs/IPFS_UCAN.md`, `scripts/browserEmailAuth.mjs`, `browserAuthServer.mjs`, `ucanStorage.mjs`, `generateUcanServiceKey.mjs` (@ucanto).
1. The browser creates an Ed25519 agent DID, stored in IndexedDB.
2. The wallet signs a statement binding wallet + browser DID + a salted email commitment.
3. The auth service sends a 15-minute single-use magic link.
4. Clicking it delegates `store/add` to that browser DID for 30 days.
5. Each upload uses a fresh 5-minute invocation, and the service exchanges it for a short-lived Pinata upload URL.

### Plan (reuse-first)
- [ ] Extract ArtFi's UCAN agent and the email-auth client into a DecentHead provider: "Decent UCAN (email + wallet)". The `ucanAuth` seam is already planned in DecentHead vNext.
- [ ] Make the auth service a small shared "Decent pin relay" that any dapp can use. It holds the service DID plus the Pinata key and validates the delegation chain. **Decide hosting** (Cloudflare Worker / Deno Deploy / own VPS) and the mail sender. This relay is the one shared, trusted piece.
- [ ] Self-sovereign options stay first-class: own Pinata JWT, IPFS Desktop / Kubo, and, later, user-run relays (anyone can run the relay with their own service DID).
- [ ] Decent_NDA: UCAN delegations also grant read/decrypt rights to the counterparties of an encrypted document (ties to D7 encryption).
- [ ] BigNuten: the health snapshot backup uses the UCAN path, with data encrypted client-side before pinning (D7).
- [ ] Recovery: add an agent-rotation/re-link flow, since clearing site data loses the key.

**Note:** UCAN controls who may write and share. It does not make a CID private, so sensitive data must be encrypted before pinning.

## Goal

Extend the existing radio scheduler so a calendar block can run a custom automated playlist, either selected by rules or curated by a wallet. Community members should be able to DJ an hour by submitting their playlist and the required jukebox fees for its queued plays.

The first use case is a **Songs Awaiting Your Vote** hour: give songs that have never received an upvote or downvote deliberate airtime, invite community feedback, and let those genuine votes influence their position in regular rotation.

This is a feature specification and planning issue, not authorization to deploy changes or move funds. Product decisions listed below must be settled before implementing their behavior.

## Why this needs scheduler support

### Playlist maker and library

- A playlist contains **1–10 songs**, potentially from different artists. Enforce the cap in the UI, service, and payment contract, not just the browser.
- Add songs from NFT-card **+ Playlist**, Top 10 playlist controls, and DJuke song selection. Keep the googly-eye Watchlist button independent.

| Mode | Price | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |

items.title: Fix header: pin DecentHead to pre-v2 commit (restores ankh menus)
items.body:
## Problem
After DecentHead v2.0.0 merged to `main` (Oct 21), jsDelivr began serving v2 for `DecentHead@main`. Busking's header overrides (`header.js`, `header-right-ankh-override.js`) target the v1 component structure, so the **left and right ankh menus disappeared** (no admin/payroll/profile access), the wallet button was mispositioned and showed status text beneath it. Not caused by #249; it only coincided with the CDN's 12h cache refresh.

Verified: `curl` of `DecentHead@main/.../WalletConnect.js` is byte-identical to DecentHead v2 `main`.

## Fix
- Pin both CDN bases to `7baa1c8c47ee33a2162b4dbd4570a14108a24d53` (last pre-v2 commit; its only change was the license).
- Bump `?v=` cache-busters so browsers re-fetch.
- Regression test: DecentHead CDN imports must use a full commit SHA, never `@main`.

## Verification
- Served branch locally: all DecentHead requests resolve to the pinned SHA; both ankhs render, ankh dropdown opens, wallet is the round orbit button with no text below.
- `test/header-layout.test.js` + `test/radio-history.test.js`: 16/16 pass.

## Follow-up
Adopting DecentHead v2 in Busking is NEXT 4 work (Canopy → Busking → BigNuten) and must port the ankh menus deliberately. Never track `@main` again.
